parser_method.group_key: (current pkg header, complete benchmark name including subbenchmark and GOMAXPROCS suffix)
parser_method.aggregation: Arithmetic median separately for ns/op, B/op and allocs/op over all three reported samples; medians need not come from the same sample. Original rounded Go output is retained.
parser_method.checks: Every line starting Benchmark parses; iterations positive, timings finite/positive, allocation counters nonnegative; exactly three samples per result; stripping /subcase and -GOMAXPROCS reproduces the complete unique -list inventory.
parser_method.resources: GNU time exact-label extraction; require exit0 agreeing with receipt, argv agreement, wall time within0.1s, empty stderr, zero swaps/signals. RSS is command resource output, not aggregate machine memory.

limitations: Upstream native benchmarks are a separate Go-only inventory, including cache, reflection, pattern and concurrent APIs absent from the OCaml declared subset. Names do not establish identical paired workloads.

Many native constructors and timed Enforce calls discard returned errors and authorization decisions (model_b_test.go; enforcer_cached_b_test.go). PASS confirms benchmark completion, not checksummed enforcement correctness.

Cached string benchmarks repeat one request key and amortize initial misses. CachedABACModel and CachedWithEnforceContext use non-cacheable parameters and fall back to ordinary Enforcer (enforcer_cached.go:63-70,163-176; abac_test.go:28-37).
CachedRBACModelMediumParallel reports only 7,8,4 iterations; initial misses and scheduling can dominate these short samples. The two pattern graph-building results have one iteration per sample.

Single-rule native management benchmarks use random inputs and mix changes with noops, including formatting/randomness in timing. RemovePoliciesLarge checks removal/restoration and excludes restoration timing.

Three 100ms samples provide bounded exploratory measurements, not confidence intervals or universal performance claims. Setup can exceed benchtime; independent resource/exit receipts remain necessary.
The project paired benchmark harness separately checks exact expected checksums and process/stderr protocol for both implementations; those receipts are the supported-subset comparison evidence.
